name: Session
tagline: Focus timer with app blocking, planning, and session analytics

pricing.notes: Official pricing page reviewed; taxes, promotions, and regional pricing may differ.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited focus and rest sessions; analytics limited to the past 2 days; calendar view included.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Full analytics, planning, blocking, and Pro features.
tiers.notes: $39.99 billed yearly; 7-day trial that does not start a subscription.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited focus and rest sessions; analytics show only the past 2 days.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; 7-day trial with no subscription started
pricing.hiddenCosts: The $3.33 figure on file is the annual-billing equivalent; month-to-month Pro is $4.99. Prices can differ by region and subscriptions auto-renew; the 30% student discount lasts 1 year and does not renew.

verdictSummary: Session's solo core is compact: build a local desktop utility that captures the essential focus timer workflow with keyboard-first controls and local storage. A competent builder can reach a useful personal version in one sitting, while the paid product mainly wins on polish, OS integration.
coreLoopDIY: Build a local desktop utility that captures the essential focus timer workflow with keyboard-first controls and local storage.
replacementScope: personal replacement for the core loop
requirements: macOS, Windows, or Linux development machine
Local filesystem access and OS permissions
whyPeopleStillPay: Session: People keep paying because a utility used dozens of times a day must be instant, predictable, and compatible with every OS update.
ongoingBurden: Track OS permission changes, shortcut conflicts, packaging, code signing, and regressions after system updates.

priorArt.name: ActivityWatch
priorArt.desc: Local-first automatic time tracking with an extensible event model.

rejectedAlternatives.name: ScreenZen
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It blocks distractions well, but does not plan work or analyze completed focus sessions.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Super Productivity
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Tasks, timeboxing, focus timers, and analytics are here; app blocking is not.

notes: Strong page because Session separates a compact personal workflow from the value of long-term polish.
prompt:
Build a usable personal replacement for the core loop of Session.
Use exactly this stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a local desktop utility that captures the essential focus timer workflow with keyboard-first controls and local storage.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: cross-device sync; deep operating-system edge-case coverage; polished shortcuts and accessibility.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
